Exorcism Deaths

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In the shadows of South Africa's spiritual landscape, a sinister practice claims lives: exorcisms gone wrong. Investigating the alarming rise of exorcism-related deaths, this exposé uncovers the toxi

Unique Selling Point:
Behind closed doors, South African exorcisms turn deadly. This investigation exposes the dark underbelly of traditional healing and charismatic churches, where desperation meets brutality, claiming innocent lives

Summary:
A KZN family demands justice after the death of their 17-year-old daughter in 2022.
Prior to her death, Thozama Sonjica's family suspected that her uncharacteristic disobedience and
bad behaviour was beyond teenage misbehaviour. They suspected that she, along with her group of
friends, may be possessed by demonic forces. The families of the friend group decided to consult a
local pastor who confirmed their worst fears – the devil was at work.
The pastor ordered that an exorcism be performed on the children and vowed to do his best to help.
He got some church members to be part of the rituals and over the next few days, even families
participated in prayer sessions. Little did the families know that the exorcism would escalate from
songs and prayers to assault and torture of the young girls.
Five days later, Thozama was dead and her four friends who survived the gruesome experience were
rescued by police. The pastor and church members were arrested, and the families expected to be
notified of the progress in the case and to be called upon to witness the subsequent trial.
Thozama's family shocked when, about 2 weeks ago, they bumped into the suspect pastor, walking
free. The family had received no communication from police investigators nor the prosecuting authority
about the status of the case and the reason for the pastor's release.
They demand answers about what they believe is the pastor's early release and justice for their
daughter.

Extra Budget Items:
Flights to KZN. Bakkie hire - an hour away from the airport.

Press Release:


Pastors, Prayers and Possessions
In the shadows of South Africa's spiritual landscape, a sinister practice is claiming lives: exorcisms gone wrong. In Kwa-Zulu Natal, one family is demanding justice after the tragic death of their 17-year-old daughter. Prior to her death, Thozama Sonjica's family suspected that her uncharacteristic disobedience and bad behaviour signalled something far more sinister. They suspected that she, along with her group of friends, may be possessed by demonic forces. The local pastor confirmed their worst fears – the devil was at work – and he ordered an exorcism be performed on the children. But during the ritual, something went horribly wrong. Five days later, Thozama was brutally beaten and, succumbed to her injuries. But this isn’t an isolated incident in South Africa. Carte Blanche goes inside the secretive world of so-called Exorcisms.
Producer: Busisiwe Gumede-Chizhanje | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Behind closed doors, South African exorcisms turn deadly. This investigation exposes the dark underbelly of traditional healing and charismatic churches, where desperation meets brutality, claiming innocent lives
metadata.Summary: A KZN family demands justice after the death of their 17-year-old daughter in 2022. Prior to her death, Thozama Sonjica's family suspected that her uncharacteristic disobedience and bad behaviour was beyond teenage misbehaviour. They suspected that she, along with her group of friends, may be possessed by demonic forces. The families of the friend group decided to consult a local pastor who confirmed their worst fears – the devil was at work. The pastor ordered that an exorcism be performed on the children and vowed to do his best to help. He got some church members to be part of the rituals and over the next few days, even families participated in prayer sessions. Little did the families know that the exorcism would escalate from songs and prayers to assault and torture of the young girls. Five days later, Thozama was dead and her four friends who survived the gruesome experience were rescued by police. The pastor and church members were arrested, and the families expected to be notified of the progress in the case and to be called upon to witness the subsequent trial. Thozama's family shocked when, about 2 weeks ago, they bumped into the suspect pastor, walking free. The family had received no communication from police investigators nor the prosecuting authority about the status of the case and the reason for the pastor's release. They demand answers about what they believe is the pastor's early release and justice for their daughter.
